brief.headline: Software and services, at 9.6% of revenue, carried 257.8% of the revenue movement while new electric vehicle revenue fell $522.00M and regulatory credits fell $136.00M, and the risk section was rewritten in the same filing to name software and services markets as competitive.

threads.title: Where the revenue moved
threads.reading: Software and services grew from $476.00M to $1.55B, a $1.07B increase carrying 257.8% of the total revenue movement while making up 9.6% of the prior-period base — 26.9x its weight, the highest concentration any check on this page flagged (Revenue composition, Class A, 10-K filed 2026-02-12). A component that carries more than the whole movement means other lines ran the other way, and the same check reports them: new electric vehicles down $522.00M and regulatory credits down $136.00M. The two lines tied to vehicle sales both fell in the period the software and services line more than covered them.
supporting: The company's stated consolidated revenue of $1.66B for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, described in the release as a 27 percent increase over the same quarter of the prior year, matched the figure reported to the SEC exactly — 0.00% difference (Management claims check, Class B release measured against Class A figures).
The financial condition check found nothing crossing a threshold, and the restatement check found nothing either (Class A).
Software and services more than tripled year over year, from $476.00M to $1.55B, read from the annual disaggregation of revenue schedule (Revenue composition check, Class A).
against: New electric vehicle revenue fell $522.00M over the same period (Revenue composition check, Class A, disaggregation of revenue schedule).
Regulatory credits fell $136.00M over the same period (same check, Class A).
The line carrying the movement is 9.6% of revenue but 257.8% of the change — 26.9x its weight, flagged high severity (Revenue composition check, Class A).

threads.title: Risk language moved with the mix
threads.reading: Of 55 risk factors the filing added 3, removed 6, modified 46 and left 6 unchanged. Two changes read as rewrites in place rather than genuine departures: the removed 'The automotive market is highly competitive' is matched by an added factor covering 'the automotive and value added software and services markets in which we operate', and the removed 'Our business could be adversely affected by trade tariffs' is matched by an added 'Our business has been and may continue to be adversely affected by trade tariffs or other trade barriers'. The competition rewrite sits in the same filing whose revenue check shows software and services carrying the movement; the tariff rewrite moves the same subject from conditional to realized.
supporting: The added competition factor extends to software and services markets — the disclosure language tracks the line the revenue composition check shows growing (Filing language and Revenue composition checks, both Class A).
The section was actively revised rather than carried forward: 46 of 55 factors modified, only 6 unchanged (Filing language check, Class A).

Four factors were substantially rewritten, including consumer demand and retention at 23% overlap and EV adoption at 9% overlap — near-total rewrites rather than boilerplate (Filing language check, Class A, 10-K filed 2026-02-12).
against: The tariff factor moved from conditional to realized — 'could be adversely affected' in the 10-K filed 2025-02-24 against 'has been and may continue to be adversely affected' in the 10-K filed 2026-02-12 (Filing language check, Class A).

Six factors were removed, including 'We are subject to risks associated with our joint venture with the Volkswagen Group' and one on continuing to incur and manage significant cost of revenues, operating expenses and capital expenditures; the material shows no added factor covering either subject (Filing language check, high severity, Class A).

A factor was added on dependence on establishing and maintaining relationships with vendors and suppliers necessary for production, appearing in the same filing whose revenue check shows new electric vehicle revenue down $522.00M (Filing language and Revenue composition checks, Class A).

threads.title: Safety record beside the software line
threads.reading: The safety check recorded six campaigns between 2025-06-11 and 2026-08-06, out of 13 on record for the registrant. Two carry the same description — one or both front turn signals may fail to illuminate and flash: 25V387000 on 2025 R1S and R1T reported 2025-06-11, and 26V508000 on 2025-2026 R1S and R1T reported 2026-08-06, fourteen months later and extended into the 2026 model year. The window also holds a Hands-Free Highway Assist software campaign for failing to correctly identify a lead vehicle (25V585000) and a High Voltage Distribution Box grounding fault that may cause loss of drive power (25V537000), both on the software and electrical side of the vehicle.
supporting: A Federal Register notice dated 2026-07-06 records a granted petition for decision of inconsequential noncompliance for Rivian Automotive, LLC (Federal Register, listed Class A in the corroborating feed).

The NHTSA descriptions are narrowly scoped — named model years, a named software version threshold of 2025.18.30, and in one case only vehicles that previously had service performed (Safety record check, Class A).
13 campaigns are on record in total for the registrant across the whole NHTSA history held (Safety record check note, Class A).
against: The same front turn signal defect description appears in two campaigns fourteen months apart, the later covering 2025 and 2026 model years — 25V387000 reported 2025-06-11 and 26V508000 reported 2026-08-06 (Safety record check, Class A, NHTSA).

Two 2025 campaigns concern drive power and driver assistance: an HVDB grounding fault that may cause loss of drive power, 25V537000 reported 2025-08-21, and Hands-Free Highway Assist software that may fail to correctly identify a lead vehicle, 25V585000 reported 2025-09-08 (Safety record check, Class A).

Seat belt retractor bolts that may be improperly tightened, 26V009000 reported 2026-01-15, and a suspension toe link that may have been reassembled incorrectly during prior service, 26V003000 reported 2026-01-05, were both reported in January 2026 (Safety record check, Class A).

brief.corroboration: There is very little corroborating material here: no news or community items were collected for this registrant at all, leaving two Federal Register notices (labelled Class A in the corroborating feed) and a list of recent SEC filings. The only Class B item, the 2026-07-30 earnings release, matched the filed revenue figure exactly. With no Class B-F press or community material, nothing on this page points anywhere the filings do not — which is an absence of contradiction, not confirmation.
not_checked: 9 of 10 management claims were not testable against a filed figure; only consolidated revenue for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 could be matched (Management claims check).
No news or community sources returned anything for this registrant, so there is no outside material to set against the filings.

The financial condition and restatement checks report only that nothing crossed a threshold and supply no figures, so profitability, cash position and any prior-period revisions cannot be characterized from this material.
Revenue composition was read from the annual disaggregation schedule only; no interim period composition was checked.
NHTSA coverage is scoped to make 'rivian', model years 2024-2026, so campaigns outside that scope are not reflected beyond the count of 13 on record.
Several risk factor excerpts are truncated mid-sentence in the material, including the added supplier-dependence factor and two of the removed factors, so their full text could not be read.
The filing feed lists a 10-Q filed 2026-07-30 and a cluster of Form 4 and Form 144 filings dated 2026-08-18 to 2026-08-21, but their contents were not part of any check.
